The Necromancer Aguirre had long been fascinated by the mysterious Namtaru. In a great cave near the city of Nar-Ishkun, Aguirre found a dozen or so Namtaru, and he watched these silent, spider-like creatures build their nest. He soon discovered that the giant web they wove was far more complex and intriguing than he had imagined. The Namtaru were in fact building a kind of sundial woven from silk and moonlight. Of course, the shadow cast on this sundial came not from sunlight but from dark energy the Namtaru generated themselves. Aguirre never learned what the strange sundial was meant to measure, but he began to suspect that the Namtaru shared a hive mind — which meant there might be a “queen.” From then on, Aguirre was utterly obsessed with the mysterious Namtaru Matriarch.

Duke Istvan loved his freedom and was a constant thorn in the Angels' side until the day he died. When they presented him with the Sword of the Griffin, he hung it on the wall as a decoration and never used it again. He had the finest smith in the duchy forge him a new sword. The Iron Feather is a symbol of the Griffin Duchy's combative nature. The blade itself was forged in a shrine of Ylath, while the hilt was made in the name of Elrath. Since his descendants all bore the Sword of the Griffin out of devotion to Elrath, the Iron Feather has passed to the family's second sons ever since. The wild Pao Islands are home to many dangerous creatures. The most dangerous of all is the Pao-Kai, arguably a distant cousin of the Wyverns of the northern steppes. As the saying goes, “Wherever there is water, there are Naga and pirates.” Pirates are ruthless brigands, guilty of robbery, theft and plunder. Pirate crews elect their captains, who then sit on the Pirate Council and make decisions by vote. The council is presided over by an elected “Pirate King”, who is also supreme commander of the pirate fleet in times of war. As proof of his executive authority, each new Pirate King inherits the Sword of the Pirate King from his predecessor, a sword forged by Bradsmith of Fallhammer. Places of tragedy are often where powerful artifacts appear, and the Staff of Crystal Roses is no exception.
